published_statement:
READ, verbatim from the OCR text (garbled glyphs kept as printed):
- Abstract (p.8): 'In perturbation theory the total charge corresponding to such currents seems to be still conserved, but here it is shown that nonperturbative ef- fects can give rise to interactions that violate the charge conservation. One consequence is baryon and lepton number nonconservation in V-A gauge theories with charm.'
- Action (p.8): 'The solution has S = £{A} d'x=-82/g. (6)' [read: |S| = 8 pi^2/g^2].
- Leading exponential (p.9): 'From Eq. (6) it follows that the exponent equals exp(-82/g), (17) which explains why we get results that are unob- tainable through ordinary perturbation expansions with respect to g².'
- Axial charge (p.9): 'A configuration in Minkowsky space with n = 1 would be associated with a violation of axial charge conservation: ... AQS = 2N. (12)' [Delta Q5 = 2N for N doublets].
- Effective vertex (p.10): 'geff Cg exp(-8/g")&+H.c., (22) where is a 2N fermion interaction'; 'I have found that the constant in Eq. (22) can be computed analytically to zeroth order in g. The calculation is lengthy and will be discussed in a separate publication.'
- Weinberg-Salam application (p.10): 'All currents that are coupled to gauge fields are anomaly free, hence the model is renormalizable. But the baryon and lepton currents have anomalies. We find that one Euclidean-gauge soliton gives AE=AM=1, Au + Ad=3, Au' + As = 3, (24) where E is the electron number, M is the muon number ... Thus, because of the Cabibbo rotation, a proton and a neutron (two baryons equal six quarks) may annihilate to form two antileptons, one of elec- tron and one of muon type.'
- Suppression (p.10): 'The factors exp(-16m2/g2)= exp(-4×137 xsin 0) in the cross sections and lifetimes will make none of the predicted effects observable if the Weinberg angle is not very small.' [read: exp(-16 pi^2/g^2) = exp(-4 pi x 137 x sin^2 theta_W); the re-derivation shows the pi is required, script (b)].
- Note added (p.11): 'There is al- so a power of the coupling constant g in front of the exponent. The full details will be published soon.'
The tree's use (massform.py:1088-1090): SOURCES['tHooft'] = ('CITED', 'cited as ref [20] in hep-ph/9603208 and ref [43] in CMS 1805.06013; not on arXiv; not read'); THOOFT_VERTEX 'The anomaly vertex per the READ rule: one (q q q l) per generation' (:2054-2055); the exponent enters via RS96 eq. (2.8), now re-read: 'In the electroweak theory, the tunneling probability is unobservably small, Gamma_inst ∝ exp(-4π/α_W) ∼ 10^-170, (2.8) where α_W = g^2/4π = α/sin^2θ_W = 1/29.' (RS96 PDF p.7), which matches the tree's RS96-2.8 capture (massform.py:1078-1083) apart from '∝' captured as '~'.
published_hypotheses: H-EUCL (analytic continuation), p.9: 'Let us assume then that all Green's functions in Minkowsky space can simply be obtained from the Euclidean ones by analytic continuation.'

H-SEMI (one-soliton saddle, leading exponential), p.8/p.9: 'the leading expo- nential of the tunneling amplitude is exp(-pdx)'; 'We perform the perturbation expansion around those values of the fields where the exponent is stationary'; 'The amplitude (in the one-EGS sector) is now formally ... (16)'.
H-T0 (zero energy), p.8: 'a potential barrier V larger than the available energy E, which I put equal to zero.'
H-MASSLESS (fermions), p.8: 'Suppose now that we have in addition N mass- less fermion doublets coupled to the gauge field'.

H-HIGGS (size cutoff), p.10: 'The integration over X is finite if the Callan- Symanzik ẞ function for g is negative and if also the ir divergence is cut off by the Higgs mecha- nism.' [X is OCR for lambda, the scale collective coordinate]. RS96 PDF p.7 adds: 'Clearly, the tunnelling rate is still suppressed by the exponential factor (2.8).'
H-PREF (prefactor not given), p.10-11: the constant in (22) 'will be discussed in a separate publication'; 'There is al- so a power of the coupling constant g in front of the exponent.'
H-POINT (vertex), p.10: 'We ask now for an effective ver- tex that could mimic the same amplitude (neglect- ing the finite size of the ECS)'.
H-NF: the application is 'the Wein- berg-Salam SU(2) U(1) model in an often cited form' with electron and muon doublets and u,d_C / u',s_C quarks (two generations, 'with charm').
H-SCALE: the primary evaluates the exponent with the fine-structure constant 137 and sin^2 theta_W; no renormalisation scale is stated. (Computed: that is the Thomson-limit alpha.)
hypothesis_drift: CARRIED, massform.py:1088-1090. The tree marks 't Hooft CITED and 'not read'; it claims nothing from the primary beyond the RS96 restatement. Now that the primary is read, nothing the tree attributes to it is contradicted.

CARRIED, massform.py:2054-2070. THOOFT_VERTEX '(q q q l) per generation' is exactly the per-generation content of 't Hooft eq. (24) ('AE=AM=1, Au + Ad=3, Au' + As = 3'): one lepton and three quarks per generation, Delta B = Delta L = 2 at N_f = 2. The tree's (3,3) is the N_f = 3 extension; the primary states the rule for its two-generation model only, and its eq. (12) 'AQS = 2N' is general in the number of doublets (reaudit (d),(e)).

CARRIED, exponent form. 't Hooft's 'exp(-16m2/g2)' (OCR) is exp(-16 pi^2/g^2) = exp(-4 pi/alpha_W), the tree's form at massform.py:529-531 (reaudit (a)-(c)). The primary attaches it to 'the cross sections and lifetimes', i.e. to rates.

DROPPED, unnamed (H-SCALE), sharpened by the primary. The primary evaluates the same exponent as exp(-4 pi x 137 x sin^2 theta_W), i.e. with the Thomson-limit alpha. With sin^2 = 0.2312 that route gives 10^-172.91; with the tree's on-shell g = 2 m_W/v it is 10^-160.95: 11.96 decades apart for the SAME leading-order formula (reaudit output). The tree prints 10^-160.95 and 10^189.10 to two decimals without naming the scale of alpha. INFERENCE (not RS96's stated route): RS96's printed 10^-170, which the tree records as an 11.73-decade discrepancy against 1/29, is what 't Hooft's Thomson-alpha route gives at sin^2 = 0.2273 (1/alpha_W = 31.15).

DROPPED, unnamed, now quoted from the primary: H-EUCL (analytic continuation) and H-MASSLESS (N massless doublets). Neither is stated at massform.py:521-534 or 2951-2956. RS96 (PDF p.8, read) covers H-MASSLESS: 'the results remain valid for the standard electroweak theory where fermions acquire masses via the Yukawa coupling'. H-EUCL is nowhere in the tree.

DROPPED, unnamed (H-HIGGS). The primary states the size integral 'is finite if ... the ir divergence is cut off by the Higgs mecha- nism'; RS96 (read) states the constrained-instanton rate 'is still suppressed by the exponential factor (2.8)'. So the exponent is unmoved, but the hypothesis is the source's own and the tree does not name it.

ADDED, interpretive and unnamed, massform.py:2953-2954 and 532-534: 'per transition' and '(attempts) x (prefactor)'. The primary places the factor in 'cross sections and lifetimes' and gives a prefactor with 'a power of the coupling constant g in front of the exponent' that it did not compute. The tree prints no rate, so no figure is misstated.

WEAKENED (H-SEMI), massform.py:2951-2956: the S11 zero-temperature clause omits 'leading exponential' / one-soliton sector, which the primary states (p.8-9) and which the tree holds in RS96-inst ('semiclassical exponent', :1094).

data_at_publication.value_then: 1976: m_W unmeasured. READ from the primary: the exponent is written 'exp(-4×137 xsin 0)' (OCR; 4 pi x 137 x sin^2 theta_W), i.e. alpha = 1/137 with sin^2 theta_W left free ('if the Weinberg angle is not very small'). Over sin^2 = 0.20-0.40 that gives 1/alpha_W = 27.4-54.8 and factors 10^-149.57 to 10^-299.15 (reaudit).
data_at_publication.value_now: 1/alpha_W = 29.491 on-shell: m_W = 80.362 GeV from the repo PDG-2026 capture, and v = 246.2196 GeV from G_F, which is NAMED-NOT-READ. 1/alpha_W = 29.580 in MSbar at m_Z (inputs NAMED-NOT-READ).
data_at_publication.source_now: research/warp-drive/captures/PDG-2026.tsv for m_W. G_F and the MSbar inputs are NAMED-NOT-READ (PDG unreachable).
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: Not the conclusion: every value gives < 10^-149. It moves the tree's digits: 't Hooft's own route with today's sin^2 = 0.2312 gives 10^-172.91, against the tree's 10^-160.95 (11.96 decades); on-shell vs MSbar at m_Z (first audit) 0.48 decades.

data_at_publication.quantity: N_f, the number of complete generations (Delta B = Delta L = N_f)
data_at_publication.value_then: 2 in the 1976 'with charm' model (search-summary gist, not READ). The b quark came in 1977 and the t in 1995.
data_at_publication.value_now: 3, from massform.n_generations() on the repo PDG capture. LEP's N_nu is NAMED-NOT-READ.
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: No. The rule is general in N_f: rederive D1 gives (2,2) at N_f = 2 and (3,3) at N_f = 3. Only the leg count (8 to 12) and ceil(B/N_f) change.

data_at_publication.quantity: RS96 eq. (2.8) printed value (a restatement datum)
data_at_publication.value_then: 10^-170 at alpha_W = 1/29 (tree capture, massform.py:1078-1083, unverified here)
data_at_publication.value_now: The arithmetic gives 10^-158.27. Printing 10^-170 would need 1/alpha_W = 31.15 (rederive E3).
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: No. It is a discrepancy of 11.73 decades, already recorded by the tree and not repaired (massform.py:534-536, 900-903). It is not a refutation of 't Hooft, and the tree uses its own computed 10^-160.95.

rederivation.outcome: Exit 0, ALL PASS (output thooft-1976.out). (a) exp(-8pi^2/g^2) squared = exp(-16pi^2/g^2). (b) With g^2 = 4 pi alpha/sin^2, 16 pi^2/g^2 = 4 pi sin^2/alpha: the printed 'exp(-4×137 xsin 0)' must carry a pi (OCR loss). (c) = 4 pi/alpha_W, the tree's form. Thomson-alpha route: sin^2 0.20 -> 10^-149.57; 0.2229 -> 10^-166.70; 0.2312 -> 10^-172.91; 0.40 -> 10^-299.15. RS96's 10^-170 = Thomson route at sin^2 0.2273 (inference). Tree: 1/alpha_W = 29.4913, 10^-160.949. (d) eq.(24): Delta B = Delta L = 2 at N_f = 2; per generation (qqq l) = THOOFT_VERTEX unit; (3,3) at N_f = 3, B - L conserved. (e) eq.(12): fermions created = N = 8 doublets = 6 quarks + 2 leptons. The first audit's BPST construction (S = 8 pi^2/g^2, Q = 1, 23 PASS) stands and now agrees with the primary's eq. (6).

lacked_data: In 1976 't Hooft lacked m_W, a precise sin^2 theta_W and the third generation, and wrote the exponent with alpha = 1/137 and a free Weinberg angle. Evidence it does not change the conclusion (computed): every sin^2 in 0.20-0.40 gives < 10^-149; today's values give 10^-160.95 (on-shell g) to 10^-172.91 (his own Thomson-alpha route). The rule (24) is per generation, so a third generation changes (2,2) to (3,3) and nothing structural. What the primary shows that the first audit could only infer: the scale ambiguity is in the source itself (it uses alpha(0)), and it moves the exponent by ~12 decades, larger than the 0.48-8.77 decades the first audit computed over electroweak-scale choices. M's suspicion (a lacked datum moves the result) is not borne out for the verdict; it is borne out for the tree's two-decimal digits, which rest on an unnamed scale choice.
grade_evidence: READ primary confirms everything the tree uses: the exponent exp(-16 pi^2/g^2) = exp(-4 pi/alpha_W) ('exp(-16m2/g2)', p.10, OCR), and the per-generation vertex (eq. (24), p.10) that THOOFT_VERTEX encodes; nothing is contradicted, so not WRONG. It stays NARROWED because the primary itself states hypotheses the tree's S11 clause does not carry: analytic continuation from Euclidean Green's functions (p.9), N massless doublets (p.8), the one-soliton leading exponential (p.9), finiteness of the size integral only with the Higgs IR cutoff and negative beta (p.10), and an uncomputed prefactor with 'a power of the coupling constant g' (p.11). Most sharply, the primary evaluates the exponent with alpha = 1/137 ('exp(-4×137 xsin 0)'), which at today's sin^2 gives 10^-172.91 against the tree's 10^-160.95 -- 11.96 decades from scale choice alone, where the tree prints two decimals and names no scale. None of this moves a verdict (all < 10^-149; the tree prints no rate).
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names the scale/scheme of alpha_W at the S11 zero-temperature clause (or prints the exponent to the precision leading order supports, i.e. ~10^-161 to 10^-173) and names H-EUCL, H-SEMI, H-HIGGS there. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a verdict comes to rest on the two-decimal exponent. WRONG is not reachable: the exponent and the vertex are the primary's own, re-derived.
